items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Butter Beans and Suzie ... they had a circuit that, I know we played Georgia, Florida, Texas, Louisiana, and you would work split week sometimes.

ctx.x: TOBA stood for 'Tough On Black Actors'. That's what it stood for. And you know, on that circuit, I think it was a Godsend, really, for a professional black

performers at the time, because that was probably the only chance they had to work, other than working on carnivals and circuses, because they had the Keith Orpheum circuit then, and they had the Pantages circuit, which I think that was out west, but in the south and the midwest, for a black performer -- Ethel Waters came off of it, I don't know if you've heard of the Whitman Sisters and those type of people. Butter Beans and Suzie ... they had a circuit that, I know we played Georgia, Florida, Texas, Louisiana,…

For instance, in Florida, I know we would play Tampa for three days and Pensacola for three days and that type of thing, but it would be in theatres -- and the theatres would always be packed. We'd play Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Oklahoma, and many of the really, the -- as I say, Bessie Smith was on TOBA, Mamie Smith was on TOBA -- and that was when I really learned to dance.
